source_credit: Hane Studios, Cigar Room Environment (Fab); course-authored deliberately inefficient lab variant and audit tools
capture_kind: Actual Unreal editor / native Insights / locally generated audit dashboard screenshots. Not benchmark comparisons.

trace_conditions.scope: Standalone editor runtime, not packaged build; includes startup/first encounter and steady segments

images.title: Furnished lounge: Audit Camera
images.question: What appearance must the optimized room preserve?
images.show: Establish furniture, warm interior lighting, books, glass and the fixed comparison view.
images.limit: Intentionally inefficient baseline; this is not the optimized answer.
images.route: Open Lounge_Unoptimized in UE 5.7, then Audit Camera in Standalone.

images.title: Reverse angle through the seating area
images.question: Does a proposed change survive another viewpoint?
images.show: Show the opposite seating, shelves and lighting coverage.
images.limit: Different camera from Audit Camera; do not compare its timing as a matched pair.
images.route: Editor camera: (15, -100, 280), looking at (180, 100, 230).

images.title: Tabletop, bottles and small props
images.question: Which details and shadow cues matter up close?
images.show: Inspect table contents, material variation and bright local illumination.
images.limit: Close view, not an independent optimization treatment.
images.route: Editor camera: (340, -50, 250), looking at (180, 45, 190).

images.title: Frame triage and GPU queue statistics
images.question: Which measurement should guide the next investigation?
images.show: Point to Frame, Game, Draw, RHIT, GPU and render resolution; then graphics, compute and copy queues.
images.limit: Editor HUD at 866×550, with diagnostic/logging overhead. It is not a controlled baseline or a serial sum of queues.
images.route: Console: stat unit; stat gpu; stats.MaxPerGroup 8. Restore row limit 25 and stat none afterward.

images.title: Timing Insights: graphics and compute
images.question: Which passes overlap and which work extends the frame?
images.show: Read nested GPU events, queue overlap and the selected time interval together.
images.limit: Inclusive totals overlap. The diagnostic trace was capped at 60 and recorded alongside the editor; it is not a performance claim.
images.route: Open Lounge-SM6.utrace in UE 5.7 UnrealInsights. Timing Insights → click a frame → drag the time ruler → F.

images.title: Timing Insights: CPU waits and idle
images.question: Is this long CPU scope executing work or waiting?
images.show: The selected Game thread idle time scope is inside the frame/tick-rate wait. Follow callers and callees.
images.limit: t.MaxFPS 60 intentionally introduces pacing; do not diagnose that idle scope as expensive gameplay.
images.route: Timing Insights → CPU/GPU menu → hide GPU tracks → select Game thread idle time.

images.title: Light Mixer: all 33 scene lights
images.question: Which lights have oversized influence and which group should we inspect?
images.show: Read attenuation radius and intensity for Fill Lights and the source blueprint lights. Show search, selection and the solo/mute controls.
images.limit: An editing interface, not a GPU cost ranking. Restore solo/visibility after inspection; avoid bulk edits during a measured comparison.
images.route: Window → Light Mixer. Search Interior Fill; inspect a single light before editing a duplicate map.

images.title: Light Complexity
images.question: Where do multiple non-static lights influence the visible scene?
images.show: Use the legend and broad saturated coverage as an inspection lead, then inspect the actual light radii.
images.limit: A diagnostic count/color model, not milliseconds. Renderer/material paths affect what is represented.
images.route: Viewport View Mode → Optimization Viewmodes → Light Complexity. Return to Lit for timing.

images.title: Virtual Shadow Map cache visualization
images.question: Which visible areas show invalidated shadow data?
images.show: Read the actual on-screen cache legend: all invalidated, dynamic invalidated and force cached.
images.limit: This image shows the deliberately faulty map; it does not demonstrate a measured saving from changing invalidation policy.
images.route: View Mode → Virtual Shadow Map Visualization → cache. Return to Lit afterward.

images.title: Unlit
images.question: Does the base surface already explain the visible difference?
images.show: Separate surface color/material appearance from the lit result at the same camera.
images.limit: Unlit is not an optimization treatment or a physically equivalent final image.
images.route: View Mode → Unlit; compare with the Audit Camera Lit capture.

images.title: Detail Lighting
images.question: Is a problem in lighting/normal detail rather than surface color?
images.show: Inspect neutral material lighting and retained normal detail on the same room.
images.limit: This changes the diagnostic representation; do not time it as the shipping image.
images.route: View Mode → Detail Lighting.

images.title: Shader Complexity
images.question: Where should material and coverage work be investigated?
images.show: Read the legend, isolate a candidate material, then inspect target shader stats and relevant GPU passes.
images.limit: An estimate based on the diagnostic model. Instruction counts, texture latency and Nanite rendering paths do not translate directly into frame milliseconds.
images.route: View Mode → Optimization Viewmodes → Shader Complexity.

images.title: Quad Overdraw
images.question: Where can coverage and small triangles waste pixel work?
images.show: Compare coverage regions with actual material blend modes and the camera distance.
images.limit: This is not a universal Nanite cost map or a direct timing measurement. Pair it with Nanite overdraw and pass evidence.
images.route: View Mode → Optimization Viewmodes → Quad Overdraw.

images.title: Buffer Visualization: Base Color
images.question: Are the albedo inputs plausible without final lighting?
images.show: Compare the furnished room base color with Lit before blaming the light rig.
images.limit: G-buffer/visualization coverage depends on material path; translucent surfaces are separate.
images.route: View Mode → Buffer Visualization → Base Color.

images.title: Buffer Visualization: Roughness
images.question: What roughness values drive these highlights?
images.show: Follow grayscale roughness across leather, wood, metal and other surfaces.
images.limit: Not a cost map, and not every material path writes the same G-buffer data.
images.route: View Mode → Buffer Visualization → Roughness.

images.title: Buffer Visualization: World Normal
images.question: Are the shading normals producing the intended surface detail?
images.show: Inspect orientation changes and compare them with the Lit highlights.
images.limit: Color represents vector direction; brightness is not material expense.
images.route: View Mode → Buffer Visualization → World Normal.

images.title: Glass material and stats entry points
images.question: What does this actual glass shader do, and where do we inspect its compiled variants?
images.show: Trace texture channels into Base Color, Roughness, Normal and Opacity. Identify Stats and Platform Stats.
images.limit: Graph recognition capture; the lower statistics table is not shown in full. Do not infer a measured saving or target instruction total from this image.
images.route: Open /Game/Cigar_room/Materials/M_Glass. Use Stats and Platform Stats, choose the target and pass, then compare variants.

images.title: Wireframe
images.question: What geometry is present in this view?
images.show: Locate dense conventional/fallback representations and compare them with the Nanite diagnostics.
images.limit: Visible wireframe is not a direct count of submitted Nanite clusters or final GPU cost.
images.route: View Mode → Wireframe.

images.title: Nanite: clusters
images.question: How is the visible geometry grouped?
images.show: Inspect cluster boundaries on furniture and architectural details.
images.limit: More or fewer colors alone does not establish cost or image quality.
images.route: View Mode → Nanite Visualization → Clusters.

images.title: Nanite: triangles
images.question: Which geometric detail survives at this camera distance?
images.show: Compare the same assets with Lit and the cluster view.
images.limit: This is the Nanite representation, distinct from fallback geometry and collision consumers.
images.route: View Mode → Nanite Visualization → Triangles.

images.title: Nanite: mask
images.question: Which visible surfaces are using the Nanite path?
images.show: Compare green Nanite coverage with the non-Nanite window regions and inspect their material assignments.
images.limit: A non-Nanite surface may be intentional; translucent glass requires an appropriate representation.
images.route: View Mode → Nanite Visualization → Mask.

images.title: Nanite: overdraw
images.question: Where does overlapping Nanite geometry need investigation?
images.show: Inspect the actual Nanite overdraw visualization, then check relevant GPU work and image requirements.
images.limit: Different geometry/cost diagnostic from conventional Quad Overdraw; do not treat their colors as the same scale.
images.route: View Mode → Nanite Visualization → Overdraw. This capture uses the recorded alternate look-at direction.

images.title: Render Resource Viewer
images.question: Which GPU resource allocations deserve investigation?
images.show: Inspect named Nanite, VSM, distance-field and Lumen resources; explain the active Resident/Transient filters.
images.limit: The displayed 2747 MB is a filtered editor snapshot, not total device VRAM usage, packaged memory or project asset size.
images.route: Tools → Render Resource Viewer. Refresh, inspect filters, then search resource names/owners.

images.title: Custom optimization overlay
images.question: Which authored conditions warrant a closer look?
images.show: Show candidate bounds on the furnished scene, then identify the rule and observed property in the dashboard.
images.limit: Candidate bounds are neither shaded-pixel counts nor proven savings. The overlay itself adds diagnostic work.
images.route: Tools → Week 10 Optimization → Toggle Custom Optimization View.

images.title: Overlay disabled: timing state
images.question: Have we restored the scene for a fair measurement?
images.show: Show the same Audit Camera without candidate bounds.
images.limit: This is a reset state, not an optimized treatment.
images.route: Toggle the overlay off, restore Lit and match capture settings before timing.

images.title: Custom validation dashboard
images.question: Can we trace a warning to a specific actor, property and next test?
images.show: Use the generated 376-candidate report, filter rules and inspect the observation/policy/next-check fields.
images.limit: Snapshot of the loaded editor world. A finding is not a measured runtime cost, and unloaded/runtime-spawned content is outside this scan.
images.route: Tools → Week 10 Optimization → Validate and Generate Dashboard. Open Saved/Week10Optimization/index.html.

images.title: Editor context and source level
images.question: Are we in the correct furnished map?
images.show: Confirm Lounge_Unoptimized, 222 actors and the actual room before the session.
images.limit: UI layout is illustrative; the clean PNGs are better for projection.
images.route: Open Week10Assessment.uproject; verify DX12 SM6 in the startup log.

images.title: Return to the original Lit view
images.question: Have diagnostic modes been restored?
images.show: End the demonstration with the original room and a clear one-change investigation.
images.limit: No optimization treatment was applied or saved during these captures.
images.route: Restore Lit, clear Nanite/VSM visualizations, disable the overlay and keep the reference unchanged.
